nodes.text: Let $0=a_0<a_1<a_2<\cdots$ be the sequence of integers defined by $a_0=0$ and $a_1=1$, and $a_{k+1}$ is the smallest integer $n$ for which the number of solutions to $a_i+a_j \leq n$ (with $0\leq i\leq j\leq k$ and $j\geq 1$) is $<n$. Is the number of solutions to $a_i+a_j \leq x$ equal to $x+O(x^{1/4+o(1)})$?

#954 : [Er77c,p.71] number theory This sequence was constructed by Rosen. Note that the number of solutions to $a_i+a_j\leq x$ is always at least $x$ by construction, but Erdős and Rosen could not even prove whether it is at most $(1+o(1))x$.
